title: The Processes: Starting Up, Directing and Initiating a Project

header.html: Explain the purpose, objectives and context of the processes starting up a project, directing a project and initiating a project; explain where the seven processes fit across the project life
the official PRINCE2 7 Foundation syllabus (PeopleCert), learning outcome 5

html:
1The seven processes

The processes take the project from start to close. There are seven:

# Process Short idea
1 Starting up a project Is there a viable and worthwhile project?
2 Directing a project The board decides, runs throughout
3 Initiating a project Build solid foundations
4 Controlling a stage Day-to-day control of a stage
5 Managing product delivery Link between project manager and team manager
6 Managing a stage boundary Close one stage and plan the next
7 Closing a project Confirm acceptance and wrap up

2Starting up a project

Purpose: ensure the prerequisites for initiation are in place by answering: do we have a viable and worthwhile project?

Objectives include: the project has a justified reason, the project management team and approach are chosen, and everyone knows what is needed to initiate the project.

Context: it happens before the project proper (the pre-project period). Main outputs: the project brief and the initiation stage plan.

3Directing a project

Purpose: enable the project board to be accountable for the project's success by making key decisions and exercising overall control, while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager.

Objectives include: authority for the project is in place, the board has control at every decision point, and management is supported with ad hoc direction.

Context: it runs from start-up to closure. Key board decisions: authorize initiation, authorize the project, authorize each stage or exception plan, give ad hoc direction, authorize project closure.

Exam tip

. Directing is the board's process and spans the whole project. The project manager does not direct; the board does.

4Initiating a project

Purpose: establish solid foundations so the organization understands the work needed to deliver the project's products before committing to significant spend.

Objectives include: everyone agrees what the project must achieve, why, how, by whom, and at what cost, quality and risk, and baselines are set.

Context: it happens in the initiation stage. Main output: the project initiation documentation (PID): the business case, the approaches, the team structure, the project plan and how the project is tailored.

Exam tip

. Starting up produces the project brief; initiating produces the PID. Do not swap them.

Exam tip

. The board decides at every gate: it authorizes initiation, the project, each stage and closure.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which process answers the question "do we have a viable and worthwhile project?"

  • ADirecting a project
  • BStarting up a project
  • CInitiating a project
  • DClosing a project
Show the answer

Answer: B. Starting up checks the prerequisites for initiation.

S2Which statements about directing a project are CORRECT? (1) It enables the project board to be accountable. (2) It runs from start-up to closure. (3) It is carried out by the project manager. (4) It happens only at the end.

  • A3 and 4
  • B2 and 3
  • C1 and 4
  • D1 and 2
Show the answer

Answer: D. Directing is the board's process and spans the project.

S3Identify the missing word. The [ ? ] is produced during initiating a project and baselines the project's plans and approaches.

  • AHighlight report
  • BPID
  • CLessons log
  • DException report
Show the answer

Answer: B. The project initiation documentation is the main output.

S4At which point does the board decide to authorize the project?

  • ABefore starting up a project
  • BAfter closing the project
  • CDuring every checkpoint report
  • DAfter initiating a project
Show the answer

Answer: D. The board authorizes the project after the PID has been prepared.

S5Which process produces the project brief and the initiation stage plan?

  • AControlling a stage
  • BStarting up a project
  • CManaging product delivery
  • DManaging a stage boundary
Show the answer

Answer: B. Those are outputs of starting up.

S6Which process establishes solid foundations before significant spend is committed?

  • AClosing a project
  • BManaging a stage boundary
  • CDirecting a project
  • DInitiating a project
Show the answer

Answer: D. Initiating sets the foundations.

5.2 Recall questions

R1How many processes does PRINCE2 7 have?

Show the answer

Seven.

R2What question does starting up a project answer?

Show the answer

Do we have a viable and worthwhile project?

R3Who carries out directing a project?

Show the answer

The project board.

R4What is the main output of initiating a project?

Show the answer

The project initiation documentation (PID).

R5What are the outputs of starting up?

Show the answer

The project brief and the initiation stage plan.

R6When does directing a project happen?

Show the answer

Throughout, from start-up to closure.

6Quick Reference Card

Process Purpose in a phrase
Starting up viable and worthwhile? (project brief)
Directing board decisions and control, throughout
Initiating solid foundations (PID)
